name: BottomNav
whenToUse: The top-level destinations of a phone app: 3–5 of them, each reachable from anywhere.

whenNotToUse.text: More than five destinations, or a desktop layout

anatomy.description: a `nav` landmark at the bottom edge, padded for the home indicator; `fixed` or `sticky`.
icon (24px) and a label; `href` makes it a link, `asChild` takes a router link.
`active`: tonal pill behind the icon and a semibold label.
`badge`: a count (over 99 reads “99+”) or `true` for a dot; on the right of the icon, in RTL too.

do.caption: Every item has a short label under its icon.
do.example: } label="Home" active /> } label="Search" /> } label="Inbox" badge={3} /> } label="Profile" />

dont.caption: Icons alone make people guess, and there is no icon-only variant.

a11y: A `nav` landmark named “Main” by default; give a second bar its own `aria-label`.
The current item has `aria-current="page"` and is marked by more than color: the pill and a semibold label.
The badge count is part of the item’s name: “Inbox, 3 new”.
Items are 68px tall and share the width, so targets stay large at 360px.
Its height is reserved as scroll padding, so a focused field never hides under it.

props.name: position
props.description: `fixed` (default) pins it to the viewport; `sticky` to the bottom of its scroll container.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon (24px). Decorative: the label names the item.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, one or two short words. Required: there is no icon-only item.

props.name: active
props.description: The current destination: `aria-current="page"`, semibold label, tonal pill.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Render your router's link instead of an `<a>`: pass it as the only child
with no children of its own, e.g. `<BottomNavItem asChild …><Link to="/inbox" /></BottomNavItem>`.

props.name: badge
props.description: A count on the icon (over 99 shows "99+"), or `true` for a dot.
